records.title: Collector grades still-PENDING (un-launched) runs as FAILED on the first sweep
records.divergence_description: collect_harness_run submits _collect_one_run_detached for every manifest entry with no state filter; a starved PENDING entry with pid=None falls into the orphan-poll 'process gone' branch and is graded FAILED, defeating the 3600s ABANDONED_STARVED deadline that exists to let it acquire a slot across later passes.
records.documented_intent: REQ-001: collect_harness_run must not assign a terminal state to a manifest entry with state=PENDING and pid is None that is within its _pending_deadline_s() window.
records.code_behavior: plan_runner.py:2606-2611 submits all entries; plan_runner.py:2123 (pid is None) → :2146 sets terminal=FAILED; runner.py:1043-1044 returns (None,'') for the missing stream so nothing prevents it. Executed: test_bug_001 xfails (terminal_state == FAILED).
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix, not upstream-spec-issue or spec-fix: the intent (Tier-3 code contract — the run-state machine's PENDING semantics + the 165 ABANDONED_STARVED deadline) is internal and correct; the collector's dispatch is what diverges. A one-branch guard in _collect_one_run_detached restores it. Not mis-read — the failure is reproduced by an executed test.
records.reachability_analysis: No guard: collect_harness_run's submit loop (plan_runner.py:2606) iterates every entry with no state filter, and _collect_one_run_detached has no PENDING/pid-None early return before the orphan-poll branch — the FAILED path at :2146 is reached unconditionally for a pid=None entry. Confirmed reachable by executing _collect_one_run_detached on a PENDING/pid=None entry (test_bug_001 xfails).
records.proposed_fix: quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch — add an early-return guard in _collect_one_run_detached that leaves a within-deadline PENDING/pid=None entry ungraded (terminal_state='PENDING') for the next collector pass.

records.title: Collector retry-launch path omits update_pid, leaving a phantom pid=0 slot that ages out at 300s
records.divergence_description: _retry_pending_runs_once acquires a pid=0 slot reservation and spawns the run but never calls update_pid; the reservation ages out after _PID_ZERO_MAX_AGE_S (300s) while the real run (30-90 min) is still alive, so the per-provider concurrency cap silently over-admits.
records.documented_intent: REQ-002: any code that calls acquire_run_slot then spawns a run must call update_pid with the launched PID before returning (as the orchestrator path does at plan_runner.py:3078).
records.code_behavior: plan_runner.py:2509 acquires the slot, :2530 spawns via _launch_one_run_detached, :2538 merges the entry — no update_pid call anywhere in the function. inflight_registry.py:341-348 ages out a pid=0 entry older than 300s. Executed: test_bug_002 xfails (no 'update_pid' in the function body).
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix, not deferred: the orchestrator path already demonstrates the correct pattern (update_pid at :3078) and the fix is a 4-line transcription into the retry path; there is no design tension. Not spec-fix — no documentation changes.
records.reachability_analysis: No compensating update_pid: _retry_pending_runs_once is the only acquire_run_slot caller besides the orchestrator, and a source scan of its body finds no update_pid; the pid=0 reservation therefore ages out at 300s (inflight_registry.py:341-348) with no upstream guard. Reachable on every starved-then-retried run that lasts longer than 5 minutes (i.e. essentially all real runs).
records.proposed_fix: quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch — call _inflight.update_pid(harness_run_dir, run_index=pr.index, pid=entry['pid']) immediately after the manifest merge, mirroring plan_runner.py:3078.

records.title: Relaunched PENDING manifest entry keeps state=PENDING instead of transitioning to RUNNING
records.divergence_description: _launch_one_run_detached's returned manifest-entry dict carries no state key, so the _retry_pending_runs_once merge leaves the prior state='PENDING' in place even though the run is now live with a pid; status/grouping surfaces and any state-filtered consumer then see a running run tagged PENDING.
records.documented_intent: REQ-003: after a successful retry relaunch, the manifest entry's state must reflect RUNNING (not remain PENDING).
records.code_behavior: plan_runner.py:1844-1872 returns the entry dict with no 'state' key; plan_runner.py:2538 merges it over the PENDING entry, preserving state='PENDING'. Executed: test_bug_003 xfails (no '"state"' in _launch_one_run_detached body).
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix: the run-state machine's PENDING→RUNNING edge is simply missing; adding state='RUNNING' to the launch return dict is the minimal correct fix and also benefits the orchestrator path (which writes the same dict). Not mis-read — reproduced by an executed source-inspection test.
records.reachability_analysis: No guard: _launch_one_run_detached's return dict (plan_runner.py:1844-1872) sets no state key and the retry merge (:2538) preserves the prior PENDING; nothing downstream re-sets state to RUNNING. Reachable on every retry relaunch. Severity MEDIUM (not HIGH) because the collect loop currently processes the entry anyway via its pid, so the consequence is surface/observability drift plus latent risk for any future state-filtered consumer, not an immediate mis-grade.
records.proposed_fix: quality/patches/BUG-003-fix.patch — add "state": "RUNNING" to the dict returned by _launch_one_run_detached.

records.title: _PHASE_ARTIFACTS misattributes Phase-2 Generate outputs to Phases 4/5, over-reporting progress
records.divergence_description: status._PHASE_ARTIFACTS maps QUALITY.md→Phase 5 and COMPLETENESS_REPORT.md→Phase 4, but both are Phase-2 Generate outputs (run_playbook.py:1522-1523 checks them as Phase-2 prerequisites before Phase 4 starts). Because _infer_phase_from_artifacts returns the highest phase with evidence, a run that finished only Phase 2 is reported as Phase 5 — so an operator watching a wedged run won't intervene.
records.documented_intent: REQ-004: _infer_phase_from_artifacts must key each phase on an artifact the runner treats as that phase's exclusive boundary marker, and must never report a higher phase than the one actually completed.
records.code_behavior: status.py:285-316 maps 4→COMPLETENESS_REPORT.md and 5→QUALITY.md; status.py:388 returns the highest matching phase. run_playbook.py:1522-1523 lists both files among the Phase-2 prerequisites ('run Phase 2 first'). Executed: test_bug_004 xfails (a Phase-2-only fixture resolves to phase != 2).
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix: the authoritative phase→artifact mapping is the runner's own prerequisite gate (run_playbook.py:1522) plus the SKILL artifact contract; status.py's map simply disagrees with it. Re-keying the map is code-only. Not cross-source for fix purposes — the divergence is resolved by aligning code to the runner's contract, no doc edit.
records.reachability_analysis: No guard: _infer_phase_from_artifacts (status.py:358-401) returns the highest phase in _PHASE_ARTIFACTS with a present file and QUALITY.md→P5 is unconditional; reached whenever Phase 2 has written QUALITY.md (every run past Generate). Confirmed by executing on a Phase-2-only fixture (test_bug_004 xfails). MEDIUM: observability-only (no run-outcome corruption), but it actively misleads the operator-intervention decision in UC-04.
records.proposed_fix: quality/patches/BUG-004-fix.patch — move QUALITY.md+COMPLETENESS_REPORT.md to the P2 tuple, drop RUN_CODE_REVIEW.md from P3 (also a Phase-2 output), re-key P5 to results/tdd-results.json, and make P4 non-artifact-inferable (empty) since the spec-audit triage has no fixed-path single-file marker — under-report beats over-report.

records.title: pid=0 reservation with a malformed started_at stays active forever (permanent phantom slot)
records.divergence_description: _entry_is_active returns True immediately for a pid=0 entry whose started_at fails to parse, so such a reservation never ages out and permanently consumes one unit of the per-provider cap.
records.documented_intent: REQ-005: a pid=0 registry entry must always carry a parseable started_at so the 300s age-out applies; or _entry_is_active must age out malformed-timestamp reservations.
records.code_behavior: inflight_registry.py:343-345: 'if started is None: return True' — a pid=0 entry with an unparseable started_at is reported active with no upper time bound. Executed: test_bug_005 xfails (_entry_is_active returns True for a malformed started_at).
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix rather than deferred, but the fix is offered inline (in the writeup) rather than as an apply-ready .patch because the current 'return True' is a documented intentional choice ('never mass-reap on a parse failure', inflight_registry.py:339-340) — flipping it to age-out trades one risk (phantom slot) for another (mass-reap on a transient parse glitch). The disposition is code-fix because the correct resolution is in code (treat a malformed started_at on a pid=0 reservation as stale, since a well-formed reservation always writes started_at), but the apply decision is left to the maintainer given the documented tradeoff.
records.reachability_analysis: No age-out guard: _entry_is_active (inflight_registry.py:341-348) returns True the moment a pid=0 entry's started_at fails to parse, with no later bound; reachable for any pid=0 reservation written without a parseable started_at. The current retry/orchestrator paths both write a valid started_at, so reachability is conditional on a future or alternate reservation site omitting it — hence MEDIUM, not HIGH. The latent invariant ('every pid=0 reservation carries a parseable started_at') is unenforced.
records.proposed_fix: Inline diff in quality/writeups/BUG-005.md (no separate .patch — apply decision deferred to maintainer per disposition_rationale): in _entry_is_active, when pid==0 and started is None, return False (treat a malformed-timestamp reservation as stale) instead of True.

records.title: Greedy JSON-array extraction drops a valid Council response with trailing bracketed prose
records.divergence_description: council_semantic_check._extract_first_json_array uses a greedy regex (first '[' to last ']') but its docstring promises the 'first balanced block / outermost that parses'. A valid Council member response whose trailing prose contains any ']' (e.g. 'see item [2]') fails to parse, so parse_member_response raises and that reviewer's verdicts are dropped.
records.documented_intent: The function's own docstring: 'find the first [...] balanced block' / 'find the outermost [...] that parses'. REQ-010 (Council resolution must keep the Layer-2 majority well-defined) — dropping a reviewer breaks the 3-review requirement (schemas.md §9.4).
records.code_behavior: bin/council_semantic_check.py:319 `_JSON_ARRAY_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\[[\s\S]*\]')` (greedy) + :337-343 single parse attempt of match.group(0); a trailing ']' extends the match past the array → json.loads fails → returns None → parse_member_response raises SemanticCheckError. Executed: test_bug_006 RED→GREEN.
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix: the docstring already specifies the intended behavior (first balanced array); the regex simply implements it incorrectly. The fix is a balanced-bracket scanner. Not spec-fix (no doc change), not mis-read (executed test confirms the drop).
records.reachability_analysis: No guard: parse_member_response (bin/council_semantic_check.py:268) calls _extract_first_json_array unconditionally and treats None as a hard error; the greedy match is reached for any response whose JSON array is followed by a ']'-containing line. Real AI Council members routinely append prose. Reachable on any Tier-1/2 (with-docs) run; no-op on Spec-Gap runs (zero Tier 1/2 REQs, the semantic check is skipped). MEDIUM: a dropped reviewer fails the gate's ≥3-reviews rule for the affected REQ — a false audit failure, not a code-under-audit defect.
records.proposed_fix: quality/patches/BUG-006-fix.patch — replace the greedy regex with a balanced-bracket scanner that returns the first '[...]' substring that parses as JSON.

records.title: capture_phase_yn marks P3-P6 complete from Phase-2 artifacts (false completion in SUMMARY)
records.divergence_description: capture_phase_yn's artifact-presence fallback maps P3->RUN_CODE_REVIEW.md, P4->RUN_SPEC_AUDIT.md, P5->RUN_TDD_TESTS.md, P6->COMPLETENESS_REPORT.md, but all four are Phase-2 Generate outputs. A run that only reached Phase 2 is marked as having completed P3-P6, and the non-COMPLETED post-processing only downgrades N->'-', never a false Y.
records.documented_intent: REQ-004 generalized: a phase is 'Y' only if it actually ran; the artifact-presence signal must key on a phase-EXCLUSIVE marker. The SKILL artifact contract lists RUN_*.md + COMPLETENESS_REPORT.md as Phase-2 outputs.
records.code_behavior: bin/harness/plan_runner.py:599-606 artifact map; :2240-2243 post-processing only flips N->'-'. Executed: test_bug_007 RED->GREEN; capture_phase_yn('', phase2_only_tree) returns P3=P4=P5=P6=Y.
records.disposition_rationale: code-fix: same root cause as BUG-004 (status._PHASE_ARTIFACTS) but in the GRADING path (phase_yn feeds RunOutcome + SUMMARY). The fix re-keys the map to phase-boundary markers (P3->BUGS.md, P5->results/tdd-results.json, P6->results/gate-report-latest.json, P4->transcript-only). Not mis-read (executed).
records.reachability_analysis: No guard: the artifact-presence branch (plan_runner.py:595-608) runs whenever the transcript lacks a phase marker AND quality/ holds the mapped file; the mapped files all exist after Phase 2. Reachable for any non-COMPLETED run that got past Generate with a terse/Mode-B transcript. The :2240-2243 cleanup does not undo a false Y. MEDIUM: corrupts the SUMMARY phase grid (reports a wedged run as fully complete); does not change the gate verdict of the audited run itself.
records.proposed_fix: quality/patches/BUG-007-fix.patch — re-key the capture_phase_yn artifact map to phase-exclusive markers.
